summary.text: A polar climate, letter E in the Köppen system, is one where every month averages below 10 °C, so there is no warm summer.
It comes in two types: tundra (ET), with at least one month above 0 °C, and ice cap (EF), with no month above 0 °C.
Köppen tied the 10 °C warmest-month line to tree lines, since places colder than that cannot support forests.

facts.label: Antarctic precipitation
facts.value: About 166 mm a year, a polar desert

facts.label: Mountain version
facts.value: Called alpine climate when elevation causes it

items.prompt: A remote island's warmest month averages 4 °C and its coldest −15 °C. Which climate type is it?

options.label: Ice cap climate
Tundra climate
Cold desert climate
Not polar, since it has a summer

items.explain: All months are below 10 °C, so it is polar; at least one month is above 0 °C, which makes it tundra rather than ice cap.

items.prompt: In a place where no month ever averages above 0 °C, what happens to snow and ice over time?

options.label: It melts away each short summer
It turns into tundra grassland
It builds up until it flows elsewhere
It blows away and leaves bare rock

items.explain: In an ice cap climate no plants grow and ice gradually accumulates until it flows or slides elsewhere.

items.prompt: The North Pole sits on ice over the Arctic Ocean. Why is it not the coldest spot in the Northern Hemisphere in winter?

options.label: The ocean water beneath stays relatively warm
It gets sunlight all through the winter
Warm winds from the tropics reach it daily
Its thick ice gives off heat as it forms

items.explain: Arctic ocean water can never fall below −2 °C, and this relatively warm water keeps the North Pole from being the hemisphere's coldest place.

items.prompt: Antarctica is technically classed as a desert. Why does so little precipitation reach most of it?

options.label: Sea ice soaks up all the rain offshore
Its high mountains block the summer sun
The air is too warm for snow to form
Weather fronts rarely reach far inland

items.explain: Antarctica averages about 166 mm of precipitation a year because weather fronts rarely penetrate far into the continent.

items.prompt: A high mountain far from the poles has no month averaging 10 °C. What is this climate called?

options.label: Subtropical climate
Maritime climate
Alpine climate
Rain shadow climate

items.explain: When the cold comes from elevation rather than latitude, the climate is referred to as alpine, and it can mimic tundra or ice cap.

items.prompt: Using Köppen's rule, a valley's warmest month averages 8 °C. Could a forest grow there?

options.label: Yes, if the winters are mild enough
No, it is below the tree line threshold
Yes, but only of coniferous trees
Only if the valley gets heavy rain

items.explain: Köppen found that places whose warmest month averages below 10 °C cannot support forests.
